top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, sole laureate) is the stronger recommendation on the common criteria. From public knowledge and translated reception, not a full reading or independent verification, he has a voice hard to confuse with any other, formal and linguistic ambition sustained at very large scale, and imaginative depth that builds memory, the body and dream into one metaphysical project. Blinding (the first volume of the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid are the demonstrated peak. Attribution is clean: one author, one principal language. Round 2 narrowed the citation to the prose, and I would not name poetry or essays without a direct reading. Uncertainties remain: how much Romanian rhythm and syntax survives translation, and whether Solenoid and the later novels transform the project or only elaborate it. The committee's unequal competence in Arabic and Spanish limits the comparison with Adonis and Zurita, and that is a limit on confidence, not a verdict against them. The six-of-six support is not evidence of merit. P000 ranks below because the case is serious enough to warrant an award, and a citation anchored in the demonstrated peak is defensible.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; the profile lists no tie to Cărtărescu. My own dream-logic novel Den svarta månens år (2021) is context, not evidence of preference, and is disclosed but not adjudicated.
